title: ADR-165 — Original observation capability selection

action: Keep exact cluster identities and source validation; measure one reconciler for catalog changes, generate scoped RBAC from declared clusters, and qualify change/rollback before adding more fixed slots.

title: ADR-186 — Operation-scoped public role proof
provenance: Engineering response to measured excessive proof repetition; role-per-operation isolation is not an explicit user requirement.
qualification: Native continuation18 provisioned all historical66 roles; unit request-count regressions pass.

questions.q1: Runs12/13 stopped on role2: approximately141 API requests per role exceeded the five-second window.
questions.q2: No evidence user required repeating the same native proof for each narrow login.
questions.q3: Every install or credential-layout provisioning operation.
questions.q4: No comparable-project case for this many per-role native proofs established here.
questions.q5: No new privileges; an administrator still creates roles through protected installer inputs.
questions.q6: Opening, post-SQL proof, completion and unknown claim states must coordinate one retained operation.
questions.q7: No user-facing knob; five-second operation and role inventory dictate behavior.
questions.q8: Depends on API throttling and PostgreSQL lock duration.
questions.q9: Minimal fixture reduced141 to about56 requests per role; aggregate installed-role cost remains unmeasured here.
questions.q10: Fresh install qualified; immutable role-layout migration is not.
questions.q11: Provision fewer trust-boundary roles under one reviewed installer plan and batch immutable inventory checks.

rationale: Proof reuse is a valid local fix, but optimizes a high-cost role graph instead of justifying its granularity.
action: Retain the scoped operation until role inventory is redesigned; compare a small set of privilege boundaries and one installer proof per bounded batch, preserving exact grants and transaction checks.

title: ADR-187 — Replay after the guard bridge
provenance: Engineering repair for guard-generation pinning; replayable Helm upgrades support the explicit installation goal.
qualification: Native continuation23 passed completed hook/continuation replay with unchanged guard and journal.

questions.q1: Helm upgrade always failed after bridge generation advanced; deterministic design defect.
questions.q2: No accepted requirement to make completed installation unreadable after its own guard transition.
questions.q3: Normal upgrade/replay path.
questions.q4: Idempotent desired-state reconciliation is the relevant comparison; detailed external review is separate.
questions.q5: Read-only bridge reconstruction adds no runtime authority; credential inbox cleanup remains privileged.
questions.q6: Original, probe and retained phases plus partial/complete replay need different effect rules.
questions.q7: No new setting; exact phase/template machinery requires code maintenance.
questions.q8: Depends on live policy generations and retained journal object identities.
questions.q9: Adds one journal and policy GET to passive reads; cumulative installer proof cost remains larger.
questions.q10: Completed replay tested; partial replay after worker launch explicitly outside scope.
questions.q11: One versioned reconciler with explicit completed checkpoints could avoid phase-specific readers.

rationale: The fix is necessary under the present bridge, but completed replay alone is not an upgrade protocol.
action: Keep the regression and read-only/effect distinction; replace the bridge-specific replay branches when introducing a versioned, resumable installer. Prioritize recovery from partial completion.

title: ADR-188 — Configuration role proof after the SQL locks and the bridge
provenance: Engineering decision addressing measured proof cost and normal controller status writes.
qualification: Runs19–22 failed; continuation23 passed post-lock proof reuse and controller settling.

questions.q1: First configuration role failed when legitimate Deployment status updated during its exact-resourceVersion proof.
questions.q2: No documented user requirement to treat ordinary controller status changes as configuration tampering.
questions.q3: Normal installation after controllers are ungated.
questions.q4: No equivalent exact-resourceVersion settle requirement established for comparable installers.
questions.q5: No new privilege; CREATE ROLE retains administrator/root checks.
questions.q6: Opening/latest/rechecked proofs plus two-minute settling and uncertain one-use claims add branches.
questions.q7: Two stable reads one second apart and two-minute limit tune the workaround.
questions.q8: Depends on controller backoff, status churn and API/SQL timing.
questions.q9: Fixture118 requests/4.55s became83/3.25s per role; final verification85 versus120 requests.
questions.q10: Completed replay qualified, but ordinary rollout/version migration remains separate.
questions.q11: Pin security-relevant spec/UID/generation rather than unrelated status resourceVersion where safe.

rationale: Waiting for status quiescence compensates for overbroad identity comparison and still leaves high proof cost.
action: Separate policy/spec changes from controller-owned status, with mutation-negative tests. Unify configuration/public role operations after reducing role granularity; keep current post-lock protection until replacement is qualified.

title: ADR-189 — Installed permission stream
provenance: Mixed: Kubernetes-managed permissions and audit are explicit; SQL stream/epochs, two purposes and supervising lane are engineering mechanisms.
qualification: Continuation26 qualified fresh acknowledged stream; epoch/restart components exist. Finite permission-audit cleanup still identified as prerequisite.

questions.q1: Installed eligibility always failed because no product process produced the accepted permission stream.
questions.q2: User selected configurable Kubernetes permissions; not every freshness/epoch mechanism was separately required.
questions.q3: Every authorized capture or download depends on this path.
questions.q4: Kubernetes-backed permission reconciliation has precedent; exact stream/audit protocol comparison remains open.
questions.q5: Worker gains binding/source reads, narrowly denied probe-create and two SQL logins plus audit prefix.
questions.q6: Initial review, suspended epoch, unavailable source, pending audit and restart backoff require scrutiny.
questions.q7: Delegations are product policy; restart/lease timing is implementation-only.
questions.q8: Depends on watches, SQL, S3 and Transit; failure can block otherwise healthy capture paths.
questions.q9: Continuous source reconciliation and audit scale with bindings/changes; no production rate or WAL measurement here.
questions.q10: Restart covered; delegation-guard revision and finite audit cleanup remain gaps.
questions.q11: Compose the existing permission service; avoid inventing another evaluator or duplicating projection secrets.

rationale: This closes a real product authority gap. Keep its role, but do not treat rapid stream refresh or all audit state as immutable requirements.
action: Complete bounded history cleanup and change recovery, then measure permission-update latency and steady-state reads jointly with capture/download budgets before adding more probes.

title: ADR-190 — Capacity readiness around the promoted owner launch
provenance: Mixed: bounded resource/audit use is required; launch-dependent readiness cycle, dual SNI serving and exhaustive footprint inputs are engineering design.
qualification: Promoted owner and capacity ReadyAt qualified by ADR194run9; native50 passes capacity and processing setup.

questions.q1: Capacity needed launched owner while owner startup needed capacity; deterministic bootstrap cycle.
questions.q2: No user requirement ties basic audit readiness to a particular owner launch or full resource-proof graph.
questions.q3: Every promoted installation and audited operation.
questions.q4: No comparable bootstrap cycle requirement established; compare staged ordinary service readiness.
questions.q5: Adds observation listener routing, broad workload metadata reads and dedicated namespace-probe TokenRequest.
questions.q6: Initialized-but-unready capacity, unavailable audit lanes, late projection and dual TLS routes are distinct states.
questions.q7: Numerous history/backups/footprint/proof-window inputs lack measured release defaults.
questions.q8: Depends on Kubernetes controllers, SQL, auditing providers and operator-supplied capacity qualification.
questions.q9: Per-Begin current profiles plus retained auditors; entire operational overhead unmeasured at scale.
questions.q10: First startup covered; longer retention, rotation and upgrades remain incomplete.
questions.q11: Initialize stable quotas/audit storage independently, then enable operations using ordinary service readiness.

rationale: Pinning current policies at Begin is useful; the capacity bootstrap apparatus exposes many internal assumptions as operator input.
action: Produce one measured default small-install profile and separate durable quotas from volatile workload observations. Remove the launch cycle rather than accumulating extra launch modes and routers.

title: ADR-191 — Worker projection writes under one retained bracket
provenance: Engineering elimination of repeated proofs, not a new product requirement.
qualification: Permission projection native26 passed; later installed continuation exercises related projection paths.

questions.q1: One journal read took about3s; permission claim had27ms left and failed.
questions.q2: No explicit requirement to reread the same guard graph before every CAS.
questions.q3: Every worker projection publication during install.
questions.q4: Versioned CAS with bounded observations is conventional; exact comparative study is separate.
questions.q5: No new permissions or credentials; existing role operation supplies authority.
questions.q6: One opening bracket, acknowledged CAS versions and closing policy check replace repeated branches.
questions.q7: No operator tuning added.
questions.q8: Kubernetes CAS and admission behavior remain external dependencies.
questions.q9: One handover proof plus about8 requests replaces up to8 full bridge reads; measured install scaling remains limited.
questions.q10: Unknown writes stay lookup-only; no existing-layout upgrade protocol supplied.
questions.q11: This is the smaller fix under current journals; eventual installer consolidation may remove the bridge.

rationale: Explicit ownership and CAS remove duplicated work without extra background state.
action: Retain this local simplification and regressions; consolidate its bracket implementation with the versioned installer rather than creating one new wrapper per projection.

title: ADR-192 — Capacity readiness before download paths
provenance: Engineering staged-composition decision; deterministic replay and unavailable unconfigured downloads support accepted goals.
qualification: Capacity ReadyAt qualified in continuation43; ADR194/204 later supply promoted inputs and installed download paths.

questions.q1: Bootstrap was blocked on unbuilt download services and replay minted different supposedly immutable identities.
questions.q2: User did not require all future subsystems to exist before starting capacity.
questions.q3: Every fresh install and replay.
questions.q4: No special prior-art claim; deterministic operation identifiers and explicit not-configured states are established patterns.
questions.q5: No new authority from empty paths; no download path means denial.
questions.q6: Unconfigured download, pending source, provider-prime retries and unrecoverable launch finalization remain.
questions.q7: Empty paths are a transitional state, not useful permanent configuration for full S-02.
questions.q8: Controller/provider startup behavior and SQL freshness affect readiness.
questions.q9: Removes needless startup dependency; duplicate environment and processing documents still require synchronized maintenance.
questions.q10: Deterministic replay fixed; no complete upgrade path.
questions.q11: Keep deterministic identities but fold transitional ordering into one current installation design.

rationale: The useful replay fix remains; regional worker placement and missing-product context were amended by ADR204.
action: Mark superseded ordering/placement explicitly and consolidate current source ownership. Eliminate duplicate download-policy documents or define one canonical producer before adding path variants.

title: ADR-193 — Installed federation and regional cluster enrollment
provenance: Mixed: explicit multi-cluster/outbound-only and rotating enrollment credential choices; provider recipe, fork fences and finite backing formula are engineering.
qualification: Real two-cluster enrollment, restart and exact replay pass; Keycloak issuance components and Helm cluster hook pass. Layout upgrades unresolved.

questions.q1: Product could not enroll regions without fixture roots; typical required function, not hypothetical.
questions.q2: User selected rotating regional Secret; did not choose a30-minute installer or immutable role layout.
questions.q3: All new regional clusters and credential renewals.
questions.q4: Outbound agents/gateways are comparable; exact compound bootstrap/fork/audit protocol precedent not established here.
questions.q5: Adds federation endpoint, scoped PKI/KV/audit roles, regional installer admin and one named credential Secret update.
questions.q6: Generation0/pending/active/fenced, expired bootstrap, lost replies and provider setup waits create many states.
questions.q7: Backing retention/slots/proof-window arithmetic and several provider mounts are operator machinery.
questions.q8: Depends on OpenBao auth/PKI/KV, external TLS, SQL, S3 and two Kubernetes APIs.
questions.q9: Registration/signing proofs measured1.38/3.4s later; idle credential churn and aggregate installation cost unmeasured.
questions.q10: Exact same-input replay tested; different expired bootstrap requires namespace reinstall and new role layout lacks migration.
questions.q11: Keep outbound connector and one bootstrap capability; simplify onboarding around one resumable join record and supported credential recovery.

rationale: The user goal is real; manually transferring provider records and reinstalling on expiry creates avoidable operational burden.
action: Qualify expired-bootstrap replacement and existing-install role migration before more cluster features. Compare operator-provisioned credentials or a single authenticated enrollment channel without duplicate installation journals.

title: ADR-194 — Promoted owner inputs
provenance: Engineering resolution of missing producers; promotion toggle and disabled subprofiles are not independent user requirements.
qualification: Native run9 promoted owner Ready and regional enrollment passed; native50 extends to publication.

questions.q1: Promoted binary could not start without worker, API and retention inputs that no installer produced.
questions.q2: No user requirement to preserve observation-only and partially promoted product modes indefinitely.
questions.q3: Typical installation; many branches exist solely for staged development.
questions.q4: No comparative need for this mode matrix established here.
questions.q5: Adds public TLS/OIDC, provider keys and immutable role projection checks; keeps roots out of hub.
questions.q6: Observation-only, empty topology, unconfigured workers, incomplete provider inputs and accepted mode combinations.
questions.q7: Promotion toggle and test-derived limits mostly preserve transitional paths; defaults explicitly unqualified.
questions.q8: Provider key readback, Kubernetes projection identity and catalog restart behavior.
questions.q9: Full projection byte comparisons and source proofs on startup; total resource behavior not measured by unit defaults.
questions.q10: Fresh install passed; mutable credentials versus immutable startup digest complicate rotation/upgrade.
questions.q11: One complete supported small-install profile with explicit unavailable optional features can replace transitional launch modes.

rationale: Completing input production is necessary; carrying every intermediate composition increases validation and maintenance cost.
action: Consolidate 180/182/184/194 into current installer contracts, remove unused historical modes only after inventory, and provide measured defaults plus normal credential rotation.

title: ADR-195 — Installed hub retention source
provenance: Mixed: administrator maximum retention and monotonic shortening are explicit; continuously fresh audited source and four SQL purposes are engineering.
qualification: Native continuation8 proved baseline edit/restart; native50 publication consumes retention. Installed shortening and complete cleanup are separate gaps.

questions.q1: Installed captures always failed because no accepted hub retention source existed.
questions.q2: User requires effective deletion and maximum retention, not four same-process logins or five-second source liveness.
questions.q3: Every capture, publication and read; source changes are less frequent than reads, frequency unmeasured.
questions.q4: No comparison establishes this checkpoint/catch-up/audit graph as necessary for retention enforcement.
questions.q5: Four worker SQL purposes, retention CRD watch/probes and audit signing; no additional deployment.
questions.q6: Unaccepted baseline, initial review, pending checkpoint, catch-up, unsigned lifecycle and expired source can block users.
questions.q7: Baseline is real policy; extra status sentinel and source intervals are machinery.
questions.q8: Depends on Kubernetes watch continuity, SQL, object audit and Transit; outage propagates into ordinary reads.
questions.q9: Continuous watch plus fresh proof loops and catch-up pages; actual memory/API/WAL totals at scale unknown.
questions.q10: Restart tested; installed historical shortening and retention-policy evolution need qualification.
questions.q11: Use one retained versioned policy plus durable monotonic deletion deadlines; revalidate policy at a measured cadence.

rationale: Combining permission and retention projections was a concrete simplification. Requiring rapid source freshness even for an unchanged accepted retention ceiling needs separate justification.
action: Keep monotonic effective dates and auditable policy changes. Evaluate event-driven policy acceptance with bounded stale-read semantics, retaining restrictive known changes, and consolidate same-process SQL roles where privilege analysis permits.

title: ADR-196 — Regional cluster join
provenance: Mixed: regional cluster joining and write-only collectors are explicit; copying a join record and restarting pinned processes are engineering workarounds.
qualification: Native continuation8 passed join, executor, restart and exact replay; native50 acquired regional evidence.

questions.q1: Installed catalog stayed empty and pinned templates prohibited ordinary Pod replacement.
questions.q2: No user requirement to restart the entire API process for one new cluster or rejoin for S3 credential rotation.
questions.q3: Normal regional onboarding and rotation.
questions.q4: Compare reconciled agent registration; no demonstrated need for immutable process-catalog snapshots here.
questions.q5: Adds owner L4 exposure, regional write-only S3 secret and administrator join command.
questions.q6: Partial offer, staged region, accepted join, process restart and failed immutable source reopen are distinct states.
questions.q7: Fixed slots, copied digests and several pin sets expose implementation constraints.
questions.q8: Depends on two APIs, connector PKI, object credentials, kubelet restart and hub availability.
questions.q9: Catalog digest read every second; join restarts API and later publisher/key service. Workload impact unmeasured.
questions.q10: Exact replay works; credential rotation changes startup digest and needs rejoin, and version upgrade lacks protocol.
questions.q11: Validated atomic catalog snapshots and versioned credential references could avoid process restarts and manual recopy.

rationale: The join record preserves exact identity, but immutability turns normal configuration changes into lifecycle operations.
action: Retain explicit operator trust and exact target IDs; design one resumable join reconciliation and credential rotation path, then replace restart-on-catalog-change with bounded snapshot replacement if measured worthwhile.

title: ADR-197 — Regional capacity
provenance: Mixed: multi-cluster capture and administrator capacity ceilings are explicit; distributed five-second observations, per-root slots and freshness coupling are engineering.
qualification: Regional qualification/enrollment pass named two-cluster tests and native47/50. Repeated historical runs expose availability defects, not production incident frequency.

questions.q1: Initially no regional admission; later bindings were usable only a few seconds per minute-scale discovery pass.
questions.q2: User did not select the observation graph or five-second physical-mapping interval; latest download timing clarification permits reevaluation there.
questions.q3: Every regional capture/download, including the first supported deployment.
questions.q4: Agent/gateway precedent supports outbound topology, not this exact holder/claim/federation proof graph.
questions.q5: Adds port9448, regional-capacity SQL login, namespace probe account, TokenRequest and cluster workload reads.
questions.q6: Qualification, pool revisions, standbys, source/permission freshness, child restart and demand/discovery interference multiply states.
questions.q7: Fixed16 accounts/qualification rows, one regional slot, pace and slot settings tune implementation limitations.
questions.q8: Two Kubernetes APIs, TLS routing, federation conversations, SQL and controller leases must cooperate.
questions.q9: Measured135–143 observer plus24–27 probe calls per remote observation; full-scale aggregate remains unknown.
questions.q10: Append-only qualifications/additive pool changes work; removal/non-additive changes and upgrades remain constrained.
questions.q11: Separate durable quota reservations from short-lived workload mapping; validate the requested target directly when needed.

rationale: The observed bottleneck is architectural: exhaustive discovery cannot maintain per-workload five-second readiness. Extra lanes and clients compensate for that mismatch.
action: Prototype one demand-owned exact-workload validation with durable quota accounting and a documented freshness contract. Compare with bounded retained observations before adding clusters, standbys or higher client rates; retain known-negative handling and no replacement target.

title: ADR-198 — Installed key service
provenance: Mixed: managed encryption and keeping wrapping roots out of collectors/hub are explicit; one local key-service deployment and three/four purpose logins are engineering.
qualification: Native key-service startup, TLS rejection and configuration acceptance pass; native48–50 show real wraps and verifier publication. Recovery/retirement remain unfinished.

questions.q1: Without a deployed key service every regional capture failed before source acquisition.
questions.q2: Hub-cluster administrator access to local root is explicitly accepted for small deployment; repeated probes cannot remove that risk.
questions.q3: Every encrypted capture and native download in the local-key profile.
questions.q4: Separate key authority is standard; repository compares local keys/OpenBao, not a full operational benchmark.
questions.q5: Only key service mounts root and dedicated SQL credentials; outbound regions reach9447; operator supplies serving TLS.
questions.q6: Unaccepted configuration, unavailable key service, rejected peer, lost root and unknown spent wrap are distinct failures.
questions.q7: Endpoint/roots are necessary; purpose/role inventory and immutable pins add setup work.
questions.q8: Depends on Kubernetes Secret durability, SQL, TLS rotation and operator backups.
questions.q9: Per-attempt bounded key operations, not per chunk; actual aggregate authentication/provider load remains unqualified.
questions.q10: Exact rerun preserves root; root rotation, retirement and disaster recovery are still open.
questions.q11: Keep one key boundary; complete restore and routine rotation before adding alternate key backends.

rationale: This process boundary has a concrete consequence: collectors cannot obtain the wrapping root or decrypt stored evidence. Its unfinished root recovery is more urgent than extra proof layers.
action: Keep the isolated service and ciphertext-only producer. Qualify backup/restore and root rotation, then consider consolidating same-service SQL purposes and idempotent exact key operations without exposing roots.

title: ADR-199 — One source read at each end of the executor proof
provenance: Engineering removal of redundant reads; bounded unobserved hub revocation was explicitly recorded in173/199, not instantaneous revocation.
qualification: Installed executor cold proof passed ADR196run8 after failures measuring100–120 calls before expiry.

questions.q1: Full installed proof required about145 calls, exceeding20/20 five-second minimum; synthetic71-call fixture missed it.
questions.q2: Original observation already allowed unknown change within its bound; repeating every nested read was not user-required.
questions.q3: Every regional executor cold proof.
questions.q4: No novel protocol claimed; sharing one explicitly owned observation is ordinary composition.
questions.q5: No new rights, credentials or endpoint.
questions.q6: Opening/closing source and local process confirmation remain; intermediate duplicate states removed.
questions.q7: No new operator setting.
questions.q8: Opening still depends on hub registration and live Kubernetes source/guards.
questions.q9: Removes four of six approximately15-call source reads and a closing lifecycle conversation; native cold proof then fits.
questions.q10: No wire migration; other callers retain original behavior. Broader setup still needed207.
questions.q11: This is the smaller fix; further simplify the entire setup rather than layering more At variants blindly.

rationale: The evidence demonstrates local composition duplication, and the change makes ownership explicit without an ambient cache.
action: Retain the regression and fold source ownership into one documented setup interface with173/178/207. Measure complete installed Open, not only the cold component.

title: ADR-200 — On-demand capacity refresh
provenance: Engineering workaround for short capacity freshness; the user requires bounded resources, not a durable refresh-demand protocol.
qualification: SQL demand checks and native47/48/50 sampling pass; native47 still refused final storage margin. ADR213 addresses use-time staleness.

questions.q1: Discovery made regional admission mostly unavailable; historical five-of-twelve passes depended on sampling a short window.
questions.q2: Five-second mapping freshness is labelled invariant in this ADR, but provenance is engineering and merits explicit risk review.
questions.q3: Every preview/admission/download on active regional workloads.
questions.q4: No comparable demand-table-plus-poll protocol necessity established; request-triggered refresh is the simpler baseline to compare.
questions.q5: Adds SECURITY DEFINER demand functions to preview/session roles; worker uses existing observation privileges.
questions.q6: Discovery, active demand, stale binding, waiting, thin result, failed demand and rearmed download add states.
questions.q7: 60-second demand,250ms polling,16 demands and1-second margin tune this machinery.
questions.q8: Depends on worker scheduling and distributed proofs returning within existing source intervals.
questions.q9: One full regional observation repeatedly per demanded workload plus4 SQL polls/s per waiting request; aggregate concurrency unmeasured.
questions.q10: Two migrations retain names/rearm expired demands; no general workload removal or installation-upgrade qualification.
questions.q11: Request-owned direct validation plus durable allocation may avoid refreshing inactive bindings and SQL polling.

rationale: Demand refresh improves the known mismatch but turns a foreground read into coordination with a separate recurrent worker lane.
action: Measure one complete foreground flow, then replace discovery-derived short authority with an explicitly reviewed mapping policy. Keep demand only if comparison beats a direct coalesced refresh; avoid widening effect retries.

title: ADR-201 — eBPF CPU profiles for every runtime
provenance: Mixed: first-class runtime profiles are explicitly required; one host-wide eBPF CPU sampler and supported runtimes are engineering selection.
qualification: Design only; no adapter, target isolation qualification or Asservat overhead measurement. Upstream numbers are not product evidence.

questions.q1: Per-runtime adapter proliferation is anticipated; no implemented performance incident or user frequency measured.
questions.q2: User requires profiles and restricted workloads, not host-wide sampling as the only CPU implementation.
questions.q3: CPU profiling is normal product scope; universal runtime coverage is broader than initial Go pprof delivery.
questions.q4: ADR research cites official OTel profiler and Alloy; coverage/API statements require current verification before implementation.
questions.q5: Privileged node sampler reads runtime memory and temporarily sees other workloads; workload Pods remain restricted.
questions.q6: Unsupported kernel/runtime, unattributed samples, busy node, missing symbols and dependency changes need distinct handling.
questions.q7: Kernel/runtime matrix, duration and node concurrency are necessary product limits; avoid extra compatibility modes initially.
questions.q8: Kernel behavior, unstable upstream API, JIT layouts and GPL object distribution are outside project control.
questions.q9: Host-wide CPU/memory cost and attribution scalability unmeasured; upstream1%/250MB cannot be treated as qualification.
questions.q10: Pinned dependency and per-upgrade adapter qualification planned, not demonstrated.
questions.q11: Deliver existing Go pprof and a bounded native CPU spike before promising every runtime.

rationale: Reusing a maintained profiler is preferable to implementing many profilers, but universality adds privacy and qualification scope before the first installed download works.
action: Defer production adapter until S-02 delivery and deletion succeed. Then qualify one supported kernel/runtime with real pod exclusion, local symbols and measured node overhead; expand from evidence.

title: ADR-202 — Public API exposure
provenance: Mixed: browser/MCP access is explicit; direct TLS and separate L4 service are engineering constraints.
qualification: Unit exposure checks; native50 used installed public routes through capture/case and download preparation, although full journey failed.

questions.q1: Installed UI/MCP could not be reached outside the cluster at all.
questions.q2: Public authenticated access is required; no evidence user chose permanent exclusion of TLS-terminating ingress.
questions.q3: Every installation serving humans or MCP clients.
questions.q4: NodePort/LoadBalancer are ordinary Kubernetes mechanisms; supported ingress integration remains a separate comparison.
questions.q5: One public L4 Service exposing existing authenticated TLS listener; no additional application permissions.
questions.q6: Absent exposure, wrong origin/cert and unreachable Service fail; few new states.
questions.q7: Service type/node port/origin are ordinary deployment settings.
questions.q8: Depends on DNS, TLS certificate and cluster load balancer networking.
questions.q9: Negligible new application work per request; network/load-balancer scaling not measured.
questions.q10: Exact Service rerun tested; changed Service rejected rather than migrated.
questions.q11: This small exposure step is necessary; document one supported configuration before broad gateway adapters.

rationale: This is a small feature with direct user benefit and no extra authority subsystem.
action: Keep direct TLS exposure and clear origin rules. Add a supported ingress/TLS termination mode only when users need it and trust-header behavior is qualified.

title: ADR-203 — Installed publisher
provenance: Mixed: encrypted verification before visibility is required; process-isolated publisher and provider recipe are engineering implementation.
qualification: Native48–50 independently verified, audit-acknowledged and published artifacts. Compiled-role SQL/S3 regression passes; complete S-02 still fails at download.

questions.q1: Every stored artifact remained invisible because installed publisher was absent; actual omitted retention grants later blocked it.
questions.q2: User did not require static tokens or fixture authority; independent evidence verification remains valuable.
questions.q3: Every completed capture.
questions.q4: Independent verification is sensible; exact six-purpose/provider setup is not established as minimal by comparison.
questions.q5: Adds separate ciphertext read principal, verifier-only cert and audit principal; keeps roots and producer writes separate.
questions.q6: Pending verification, spent unwraps, pending audit, expired credential and changed catalog create failure states.
questions.q7: Several provider keys/roles and credential inputs increase installer workload.
questions.q8: OpenBao authentication/signing, SQL, versioned object reads and catalog guards must all succeed.
questions.q9: Full artifact verification plus renewal and catalog polling; throughput and concurrent publication load not measured.
questions.q10: Process credentials rotate; catalog changes force restart; role-layout and image upgrade unqualified.
questions.q11: Keep an isolated verifier but share installation/controller machinery and consolidate same-process logins where safe.

rationale: Unlike every-purpose SQL isolation, this process boundary separates producer writes from decrypted verification. It now has meaningful installed evidence.
action: Preserve publisher isolation and full verification; prioritize recoverable retries and operational visibility, then reduce provider/role setup duplication without combining it with the collector.

title: ADR-204 — Installed native downloads
provenance: Mixed: authenticated native downloads are explicit. Per-download Pod/enrollment, repeated five-second policy proofs and role graph are engineering; relaxed bounded permission recheck is now authorized.
qualification: Provisioning/configuration acceptance pass. Native50 reserved one Preparing session but no worker/batch/bytes; whole-phase TLS reproducer fails at4.951s before claim/create.

questions.q1: Installed download is unusable in native50; component successes did not exercise full protected-reader cost.
questions.q2: User accepts bounded permission-change latency and does not require interrupting in-flight downloads immediately.
questions.q3: Every gathered artifact must be downloadable; this is core delivery, not an edge case.
questions.q4: Compare isolated bounded download services with short-lived workers; no evidence each4096-byte context needs a new Pod.
questions.q5: Adds worker namespace/Job rights, TokenReview, read-only S3, acquisition PKI/key authority and download-audience client.
questions.q6: Reservation, dispatch audit, one-use claim, Pending, enrollment, native attachment, batches, uncertainty and cleanup are many states.
questions.q7: Worker controls, path templates, provider lifetimes and separate client settings partly operate this machinery.
questions.q8: Kubernetes scheduling, API guards, SQL, IdP, PKI and key service all precede first bytes.
questions.q9: Actual policy: 14 observer/3 probe calls, twice per full environment gate. Ten launch gates imply 280 observer calls and a 13s ideal 20/20 wait. This is arithmetic, not native-cause proof.
questions.q10: Fresh provisioning works; existing-layout upgrade, worker replacement and installed lifecycle not qualified.
questions.q11: Use one measured bounded policy observation per request/interval and evaluate a reusable isolated acquisition service for small artifacts.

rationale: A secure download requirement has accumulated a launch protocol whose measured protected reads cannot fit its chosen request budget. More continuation stages alone do not solve it.
action: First implement the already-authorized relaxed bounded recheck contract and remove adjacent duplicate checks, preserving human scope, encryption, accounting and cancellation. Qualify full prepare-to-first-byte flow. Then compare per-download Pods with bounded pooled isolated readers before expanding download profiles.

title: ADR-205 — Installed context deletion
provenance: Mixed: effective managed deletion and finite storage are explicit; three same-process SQL duties and signed deletion protocol are engineering.
qualification: Merged PR41; SQL paging/deletion and real scoped S3 credential qualification pass. Native50 armed the deletion fault but failed download before lifecycle completion.

questions.q1: Expired installed artifacts were never removed and their charges never released; deterministic missing composition.
questions.q2: User accepts inability to erase downloaded external copies, not indefinite managed evidence retention.
questions.q3: Every expired artifact; failed cleanup and restore are operationally important but field frequency unknown.
questions.q4: Garbage collection/inventory and retryable deletion have precedent; exact signed three-role protocol needs separate proportionality review.
questions.q5: Worker gains list/delete/abort-only evidence principal and dedicated signing path, never evidence read/put.
questions.q6: Eligible, leased, partial purge, inventory complete, audit pending and release pending states preserve uncertain deletion.
questions.q7: 30-second sweep and16-row pages are internal controls; operator must supply another scoped credential.
questions.q8: Provider version/multipart semantics and policy implementation matter; SeaweedFS required a qualified method condition.
questions.q9: Bounded pages prevent starvation; inventory work grows with versions/uploads. Production sweep throughput remains unmeasured.
questions.q10: Failed cleanup is retryable; current changed templates/role pins are fresh-install-only and upgrades unqualified.
questions.q11: Keep positive inventory-before-release; consider one cleanup transaction role instead of three logins held by one process.

rationale: Deletion has direct privacy/storage value and the pager fixes a concrete starvation case. Do not postpone installed cleanup qualification for more proof machinery.
action: Complete expiry, failed purge, durable audit and charge-release in the installed journey. Preserve denied reads/writes and inventory evidence; separately assess whether same-process role/signing separation adds enough value.

title: ADR-206 — Bounded approved pod-status projection reads
provenance: Mixed: approved browser/MCP inspection is explicitly required; separate query ledger, worker purpose and four-deployment backing are engineering, not a new user-selected feature.
qualification: Component query/capacity/transport foundations exist; production composition and native query qualification absent.

questions.q1: Users need approved content inspection; no deployed query failure frequency. Current design adds machinery for a4096-byte artifact.
questions.q2: No user requirement for per-read acquisition workers, separate finite installation backing or five-second repeated probes.
questions.q3: Ordinary inspection is core; full general-query isolation is unnecessary for fixed14-field pod status.
questions.q4: No comparable requirement for four deployment-capacity proofs before a tiny metadata projection established here.
questions.q5: New query-specific SQL/key/worker purposes and acquisition authority; no plaintext disk cache allowed.
questions.q6: Pending admission, worker enrollment, one-use batch start, delivery uncertainty, joined closure, exhaustion and expiry form another lifecycle.
questions.q7: 10-second total,60-second maximum, two4MiB batches and finite guard/provider/history allowances are engineering policy.
questions.q8: Depends on four deployment guards, measured-image reports, Kubernetes workers, SQL, TLS, keys and durable audit.
questions.q9: Up to8MiB charged read work for ≤4096-byte source; conservative accounting, not measured bytes. Separate guards/history multiply cost; no installed measurement.
questions.q10: Original-install-only backing; adding extension, renewal, retirement and upgrade are unresolved.
questions.q11: Reuse a bounded isolated acquisition/delivery service with a typed projection permission and existing resource accounting.

rationale: Separate authorization for approved reads is sound; a second end-to-end worker/accounting protocol duplicates an already unfinished download system.
action: Defer production query composition until native download works. Compare a typed fixed projection within the same isolated reader/lifecycle, with distinct operation authorization and bounded output, before implementing extra guard and ledger layers. Keep the inspection requirement.

title: ADR-207 — One native proof bracket for context-start setup
provenance: Engineering reduction of setup proof duplication; original bounded unknown-change semantics are explicit in173/199.
qualification: Selected native setup and component races pass; native48–50 reach acquisition/publication. Sustained installed opening availability remains unmeasured.

questions.q1: Installed openings failed; nested registration re-read the same source and full setup exceeded its chosen budget.
questions.q2: No user demand for repeated own-credential proofs at every nested callback.
questions.q3: Every regional standby opening, not just failures.
questions.q4: Owned observations are conventional; this multi-layer delegated proof graph is not justified by prior art here.
questions.q5: No new privileges; private observation handoff cannot authorize other lifecycle purposes.
questions.q6: Atomic generation, private reader lifetime, closing proof, callback count and joined cleanup add state to optimize earlier state.
questions.q7: No public setting; observer/input count changes alter feasibility.
questions.q8: Actual TLS/exporter, SQL registry and regional/hub API proofs all contribute latency.
questions.q9: Synthetic full opening114 observer/24 probe calls measured4.706s; selected simpler native cold setup1.804s is not installed timing.
questions.q10: Private implementation change; broad native lifecycle/upgrade still open.
questions.q11: One documented connector-session validation boundary could subsume the nested process/source wrappers.

rationale: The local reductions are supported, but a synthetic4.7-second best-case setup inside five seconds leaves no usable contention budget.
action: Retain current correctness tests; consolidate173/178/199/207 into one explicit session/setup contract, re-evaluate redundant self-attestation and measure installed setup under concurrent capacity/audit work.

title: ADR-208 — Opening limiter for context-start Kubernetes clients
provenance: Engineering performance tuning after native failures; fixed20/20, later50/100 and preserving all repeated probes were not explicit user requirements.
qualification: Installed acquisition/publication observed; no causal isolation or sustained aggregate API-load qualification. Initial burst-only revision failed under retries.

questions.q1: Installed openings and audit/retention/capacity paths repeatedly exhausted local limiter budgets despite millisecond API responses.
questions.q2: User now expressly rejects unproven security machinery causing runtime problems and permits relaxed download rechecks.
questions.q3: Normal openings, audits and readiness, with retries worsening demand.
questions.q4: Kubernetes APF is server-side protection, not evidence this application request graph is efficient.
questions.q5: No new RBAC; more dedicated clients can issue concurrent requests under the same identities.
questions.q6: Cold burst, depleted bucket, independent limiter starvation and retry feedback add performance states.
questions.q7: OpeningQPS/burst and growing client exemptions are implementation tuning.
questions.q8: Depends on API server capacity/APF fairness and shared-cluster workload.
questions.q9: Each selected client allows50 QPS/burst100; several added instances increase aggregate allowed pressure. Actual total steady-state load unknown.
questions.q10: Code-selected tuning is reversible; concurrency/load and upgrade behavior not qualified.
questions.q11: Reduce repeated reads and use measured bounded policy observations before increasing per-client rates again.

rationale: Separate rate limiters isolate unrelated work but do not cap total installation demand. A growing exemption list hides cumulative cost.
action: Inventory actual client instances and measured total requests by operation. Replace duplicated proof work, select a practical bounded policy interval, and establish one installation-wide request budget before further rate changes.

title: ADR-209 — Two context-start standbys per hub owner
provenance: Engineering experiment based on a mistaken per-cluster standby assumption; no user requirement.
qualification: Withdrawn after native65; implementation reverted.

questions.q1: Preview found no standby, but guessed solution conflicted with actual per-cluster slot and setup ownership.
questions.q2: User did not require duplicate standby connections.
questions.q3: Would have affected every owner opening to address intermittent availability.
questions.q4: No comparative justification needed for retaining a failed experiment as history.
questions.q5: No new privilege, but doubled concurrent authenticated connections/opening work.
questions.q6: Concurrent setup contention and standby rejection worsened existing failure modes.
questions.q7: Two-per-owner setting was internal machinery inconsistent with installed--standby1.
questions.q8: Depends on correct hub/region slot composition.
questions.q9: Opening load doubled when both reopened; no availability benefit established.
questions.q10: Actual revert completed; no migration required.
questions.q11: Keep one standby and fix opening cost/phase deadlines; do not revive multiplicity without evidence.

rationale: The premise was false and the experiment failed; it has no current implementation to preserve.
action: Retain the withdrawn ADR as evidence, remove any active specification or comment promising two exchanges per owner, and require whole-path slot/cost evidence before a replacement.

title: ADR-210 — Installed processing changes by a privacy operator
provenance: Mixed: privacy operators/control are accepted; separate initial processing ceremony, release lane and repeated short backing horizon are engineering.
qualification: Native47–50 initialize via real authenticated console path. Restriction effects, release audit lane and browser cleanup remain incompletely qualified or absent.

questions.q1: Every preview failed because processing was never initialized; console login also lacked its SQL settings producer.
questions.q2: No explicit user requirement for a separate one-time privacy-operator action before every installation can capture.
questions.q3: Browser settings are universal; separate processing initialization/release workflow depends on operator needs.
questions.q4: No comparable requirement for an extra initialization ceremony established here.
questions.q5: Adds processing-decision SQL purpose, guarded source probe, browser observer and authenticatedCSRF route.
questions.q6: Uninitialized, restricted, release-unavailable, settings-unavailable and expired backing add operational states.
questions.q7: Processing operators are policy; one-day root interval and last-ten-second renewal constrain otherwise valid retention.
questions.q8: Depends on browser IdP, SQL, Kubernetes source and durable operation audit.
questions.q9: One extra pool per retained worker plus1Hz settings read; whole request proof cost remains material and unmeasured at scale.
questions.q10: Layout digest changes; release and cleanup absent, longer retention unsupported by current backing.
questions.q11: Accept initial processing policy as part of explicit installation, retaining authenticated operator changes afterward.

rationale: Wiring real operator control is necessary under current contracts, but mandatory initialization and backing expiry create avoidable blocked states.
action: Evaluate installation-time explicit policy acceptance instead of an extra ceremony; complete reversible restriction/release and browser cleanup, and separate retention duration from short control freshness before adding controls.

title: ADR-211 — Return a completed target query to its original standby interval
provenance: Engineering transport correctness repair; no new user requirement or relaxation of work authority.
qualification: Genuine actualHTTP2 failing-before regression; complete contextstart/mtls race packages pass. Later installed runs reach acquisition.

questions.q1: Completed query left an HTTP2 timer terminating next independent query; router also allowed concurrent frame readers.
questions.q2: No accepted behavior allows one completed query to corrupt a later operation or steal its frames.
questions.q3: Normal repeated previews then capture on a standby.
questions.q4: Explicit protocol phase ownership/deadline lifecycle is conventional; exact framework timer behavior tested directly.
questions.q5: No additional privilege, endpoint or capacity.
questions.q6: Query-busy and completed-idle transitions clarify existing states; unknown/failed queries remain terminal.
questions.q7: No added knob; original residency and all existing ceilings retained.
questions.q8: Depends on Go HTTP2 socket-deadline behavior, verified with real transport tests.
questions.q9: No added network calls; lock/reservation accounting prevents concurrent frame consumption.
questions.q10: Internal fix with preserved wire format; exact cancellation/expiry regressions cover reuse.
questions.q11: This is the minimal correction while retaining multiplexed passive standbys.

rationale: The extra lifecycle logic fixes a demonstrated transport race; removing it without replacing standby protocol would regress correctness.
action: Keep exclusive query ownership, joined completion and original passive deadline restoration. If setup is redesigned, preserve equivalent semantics with fewer protocol modes.

title: ADR-212 — Remaining interval before one-use API preparation
provenance: Engineering conservative one-second floor and passive replay correction; numeric floor is not user-selected or measured execution requirement.
qualification: Real SQL red/green qualifies locks, no effects and expired replay; native48 headroom refusal then1.095163s preparation/acquisition succeeded.

questions.q1: Native45 persisted preparation with433.731ms left, consuming one-use opportunity without starting; expired replay masked uncertainty.
questions.q2: No user requirement to permanently lose an attempt solely because a speculative wrapping reply is uncertain.
questions.q3: Slow/contended ordinary capture path; production frequency unknown.
questions.q4: Idempotent preparation/reconciliation is the alternative to irreversible one-use effects; no exact prior-art comparison here.
questions.q5: No new privilege; existing authority/process/scope checks remain.
questions.q6: Adds known headroom refusal while distinguishing expired prepared passive state and actual effect uncertainty.
questions.q7: Hard-coded1s floor is a policy heuristic, not a measured safety/performance guarantee.
questions.q8: Post-lock DB clock and actual request deadlines depend on SQL scheduling and downstream work.
questions.q9: One extra database-time read; helps avoid futile preparation but does not reduce expensive prerequisite proofs.
questions.q10: Existing prepared rows remain immutable; no schema change. Long-term recovery still restricted.
questions.q11: Keep passive uncertainty fix; use idempotent exact preparation and measured workflow budgeting instead of permanent one-use loss where possible.

rationale: The passive replay repair is necessary. A fixed headroom floor reduces one symptom but cannot make an over-budget pipeline usable.
action: Retain precise expired-row/no-create semantics and rollback error preservation. Reassess irreversible wrap/start accounting and derive any preparation floor from measured complete phases; do not treat1s as a performance guarantee.

title: ADR-213 — Storage readiness at consumption
provenance: Engineering follow-up to readiness timing; no user requirement for two-phase polling or one-second storage selection margin.
qualification: Genuine component red, full capture race10.066s green; native48 includes correction but does not establish consumption polling caused success.

questions.q1: Native47 demand sampling passed, then final authoritative storage had less than1s and refused.
questions.q2: User did not select this freshness-margin/wait protocol; no evidence accepted inconsistent replacement storage.
questions.q3: Normal requests with slow target/facts work.
questions.q4: No prior-art need for a durable background demand plus foreground two-phase wait established here.
questions.q5: No new privilege; same single demand attempt and storage read ports.
questions.q6: Hint running/joined, demand spent/failed, thin same-selection, polling and terminal cutoff require careful state tracking.
questions.q7: 250ms poll/1s margin are inherited tuning; all retained fact deadlines constrain progress.
questions.q8: Depends on another process refreshing the exact binding before every original fact expires.
questions.q9: Adds up to4 storage reads/s while waiting and no fact re-resolution; aggregate requests/availability unmeasured.
questions.q10: No wire/schema migration; component cancellation/join tests pass, installed causal benefit not established.
questions.q11: Validate requested storage at consumption directly or use a measured retained mapping policy, eliminating the hint race.

rationale: Correct within the chosen contract, but compounds the demand design rather than eliminating its tight stale-read cycle.
action: Keep current negative/identity tests while redesigning197/200 as one admission-readiness flow. Compare direct coalesced validation versus retained mappings, and remove early hint/consumption state if no measured benefit remains.
